summary.name: Internet of things
summary.one_liner: Wikipedia article describing the Internet of things (IoT): physical objects with sensors, processing and software that connect and exchange data over networks.
use_cases: learning about iot in healthcare and transport
summary.what_it_does: This is an encyclopedia article, not a software tool. It describes the Internet of things as physical objects with embedded sensors, processing, software and other technologies that exchange data over the Internet or other networks. It covers the field's history from the 1982 Carnegie Mellon vending machine and the 1999 coining of the term by Kevin Ashton to later developments. It surveys applications across consumer smart homes, healthcare, transportation, industry, agriculture, maritime, infrastructure, energy and environmental monitoring. It also notes privacy and security concerns and the regulatory ambiguity around IoT data transfer.
notable: Covers history from the 1982 Carnegie Mellon Coca-Cola vending machine to the 1999 coining of the term
Lists open-source smart home ecosystems such as Home Assistant, OpenHAB and Domoticz
Cites asset tracking as the largest single IoT application at 22% of the market
caveats: Discusses privacy and security risks of IoT devices without offering solutions
Article content is general overview rather than a guide to any specific product
